sections.overview: Pseudantechinus roryi is a name historically applied to western Australian false antechinuses.
sections.identification: DNA analyses found specimens identified as P. roryi, including type material, indistinguishable from P. macdonnellensis.
sections.habitat: The western populations bearing this name were recorded in dry, rocky areas of Western Australia, including the Pilbara.
sections.diet: A separate species-specific diet is not established for P. roryi under the synonymy proposed by the 2017 study.
sections.behavior: The genetic study found no clear biogeographic separation between sampled roryi and macdonnellensis populations.
sections.reproduction: The reviewed taxonomic study does not describe separate reproductive biology for P. roryi.
sections.ecology: The 2017 authors proposed treating P. roryi as a synonym of P. macdonnellensis. The Mammal Diversity Database currently includes it there; see P. macdonnellensis.
sections.conservation: Conservation information should be read under P. macdonnellensis where the taxon is included.
